prompts.name: atelier
prompts.prompt:
Create realistic, production-quality UI design for FreightClaimKit, an ambitious premium enterprise SaaS concept for cargo damage and shortage evidence review. One independent marketing design direction called "The Evidence Atelier". Target dimensions 1440 x 1600, desktop landing page showing hero and two distinct scroll chapters, natural ratio, readable type, generous whitespace, no browser frame. Current date 2026-10-27. Reference screenshots are moodboard material only: extract the warm-white modular container, glass evidence layers and precision line relationships; ignore all phone chrome, messaging notifications and text from screenshots. Never reproduce personal notifications.
Brand: an original fine geometric open-container/case-bracket logo plus FreightClaimKit wordmark, warm ivory #F5F2EC, charcoal #202D2A, restrained burnt amber #AC582D. Refined editorial Newsreader-style serif headline with Manrope-style readable sans-serif UI, max two font families. Not generic blue SaaS.
Hero asymmetrical: elegant large left headline "Know what’s missing. Before you file." Supporting line "A provenance-first evidence audit for cargo damage and shortage claims." Solid charcoal CTA "Inspect sample claim", quiet secondary "Request a pilot". Slim conspicuous label "CONCEPT PREVIEW". Right: exceptionally beautiful architectural 3D still life of a pearl corrugated container, subtle damaged corner, a pallet inside, three large translucent evidence sheets suspended and connected by precise hairlines; no wreckage or magical technology. Source labels: "FC-208", "Signed POD missing", "Invoice mismatch". No fake recovery figures.
Next warm stone chapter is a horizontal evidence review storyboard: BOL card, unresolved signature card, invoice comparison $2,880 vs $2,640 labeled synthetic draft values. Text "A shipment becomes a reviewable record." Next forest-dark chapter begins with a spacious three-column dossier preview with left source provenance, middle evidence checklist, right reviewer A. Chen and "Deadline: verify". Persistent "DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA" on each UI preview. Include modest visible line naming five proposed modules: Freight Desk • Freight Review • Freight Proof • Freight Signal • Freight Report. All proposed not live. Build premium material depth, soft shadows, distinctive crop and refined intentional composition. No customer logos, testimonials, certifications, live integrations, recovery guarantee or pricing acceptance. This is a visual concept not actual implemented product. Prefer grouping and dividers over excessive nested cards; avoid cramped UI.

prompts.name: theatre
prompts.prompt:
Create realistic, production-quality UI design for FreightClaimKit, premium cargo evidence audit SaaS concept. One independent visual direction called "The Inspection Theatre". Target dimensions 1440 x 1600 desktop marketing page showing hero and two story sections, readable and spacious, no browser frame. Today 2026-10-27. Attached screenshots are moodboard references for modular cargo, architectural frames, controlled analytical process and claim parties; ignore phone UI and all personal notifications. Do not copy any screenshot text.
Different composition: cinematic full-width graphite-black hero stage; cream oversized modern sans-serif typography, 2 lines "Every discrepancy. Brought into focus." positioned upper left, small "FreightClaimKit" geometric logo top left and CONCEPT PREVIEW top right, CTA "Inspect sample claim" plus "Request a pilot". Render a large beautiful matte charcoal container and pearl cargo pallet inside a thin architectural rectangular open frame, warm amber light at a single slightly displaced carton. Glass sheets orbit at precise right angles, not sci-fi holograms. No actual scanning hardware, conveyors, robot, or implied sensing capability: small caption "Evidence review, visualized". Show only two restrained source-linked labels "POD signature unresolved" and "Invoice value mismatch". Strong negative space, dramatic studio lighting, premium editorial industrial art direction, not cyberpunk, not blue.
Below: stark ivory section "From discrepancy to reviewer task." Three horizontally arranged cinematic storyboard panels: source document with highlighted signature gap, invoice rows $2,880 draft / $2,640 source, task assigned A. Chen. Every panel visibly says DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA. No deadline dates or fabricated contract text; deadline only "VERIFY — SOURCE NEEDED".
Below: muted warm gray topology illustration "Different roles. Explicit authority." Solid cube Cargo owner; connected blocks 3PL agent; outlined frame Insurer; central case FC-208; separate counsel verification bracket labeled "Standing review". Distinct shapes and fine lines, no unlabeled node clouds. Footer preview strip names five proposed modules Freight Desk, Freight Review, Freight Proof, Freight Signal, Freight Report. Max two font families; 14-16px readable UI baseline and careful spacing. No company proof, customer logos, real claims, guaranteed recoveries, live integration, made-up metrics. This is an art direction mockup, not an operating product.

prompts.name: atlas
prompts.prompt:
Create realistic, production-quality UI design for FreightClaimKit, premium research-stage cargo evidence audit SaaS. One independent design direction "The Claim Atlas". Dimensions 1440 x 1600 desktop marketing page, natural ratio, no browser chrome, generous whitespace. Current date 2026-10-27. Input images are moodboard inspiration for precise connected geometric parties and transparent evidence layers only. Ignore all phone chrome, notifications and text in input photos.
Use a distinctly different layout: warm-white technical editorial surface, quiet sage-gray map grid, deep forest typography, amber only for unresolved evidence. Large refined sans-serif headline across top "One case. Every source. Clear responsibility." A small elegant FreightClaimKit geometric case-frame wordmark at top left. Visible "CONCEPT PREVIEW" header. Subline exact "Explore a proposed evidence audit for cargo damage and shortage claims." CTA "Inspect sample claim".
Hero occupies large middle canvas: an abstract schematic cargo route (no claimed real locations or live telemetry), 3 architectural nodes: small solid corrugated cargo cube for Cargo owner on left, connected modular blocks for 3PL agent at top right, wireframe frame for Insurer bottom right. In center a large crisp flat dossier card FC-208; separate counsel bracket underneath "Standing review". Fine orthogonal connectors with readable text; no floating node cloud. Dossier has only 3 rows: "Signed POD: unresolved", "Invoice comparison: review", "Deadline: verify". No date anywhere on deadline. All UI marked DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA. A small photo evidence thumbnail may be a subtly dented anonymous carton, generated not real. Composition should feel like an exquisite financial newspaper meets architectural drawing, not shipping tracking software.
Second section subtly gray, unique split composition: left "Keep the source. Record the correction." right two large precise document fields connected by an audit-history line: "Draft value $2,880" and "Invoice line $2,640"; label both synthetic, $240 discrepancy, reviewer correction pending. Make it clear this is evidence comparison, not recoverable amount.
Third section cream, editorial product index with five named proposed module rows, each different mini-diagram: "Freight Desk — Evidence completeness", "Freight Review — Verified rules and notices", "Freight Proof — Invoice reconciliation", "Freight Signal — Reviewed packets and status", "Freight Report — Recovery and prevention analysis". Narrow footer "Proposed modules • Availability unvalidated". No fabricated ROI, live integrations, customers, security badges, universal deadlines, approval stamps or operating product claims. Use Manrope-like sans-serif and Newsreader-like refined serif only for section editorial accent, max two fonts, UI 14–16px baseline. Distinct composition, readable labels and restraint, purposefully designed diagrams with lots of negative space.
